title: Russia Strikes Dnipro Medical Clinic, Kharkiv Oil Depot, 49 Sumy Settlements — Day 1,551
detail: On May 25, 2026 — Day 1,551 of Russia's full-scale invasion — Russian forces launched a new wave of missiles and drones targeting Kyiv, Dnipro, Kharkiv, and Sumy regions, continuing the aerial campaign that began with the massive May 23–24 barrage. A ballistic missile struck a medical clinic in Dnipro, killing at least 2 people and injuring over 30, including two boys aged 3 and 6. In Pavlohrad (Dnipropetrovsk Oblast), a separate Russian drone struck a multi-story residential building, killing 5 people including a child. In Kharkiv, an oil depot was struck twice by Russian kamikaze drones; 18 people were injured across the Kharkiv region, including a 5-year-old child; the town of Derhachi was also hit by a missile. Russian forces struck 49 settlements in Sumy region, killing 1 man and injuring 4 others; a drone attack on a civilian car killed a 24-year-old man in the Krasnopillia community. In Kyiv, drone fragments damaged houses and cars. Ukraine's air defenses shot down 17 missiles and 31 drones, with 246 of 262 total drones in the combined May 24–25 wave neutralized. The strikes intensified international condemnation following Russia's use of the Oreshnik IRBM on May 24.

title: Russia Uses S-300 Anti-Aircraft Missile as Ground-Attack Weapon, Strikes Donetsk Dam Floodgates — 6 Homes Flooded
detail: On May 25, 2026, Russian forces struck the floodgates of a hydroelectric dam in Donetsk Oblast using a repurposed S-300 surface-to-air missile fired in a ground-attack role — a tactic Russia has increasingly employed to attack targets its dedicated ground-attack missiles cannot reach or have been depleted against. The strike directly hit the floodgates on the Vovcha River, threatening the villages of Halytsynivka, Zhelanne-1, and Zhelanne-2. Six homes were flooded and 26 civilians were evacuated. The tactic of repurposing Soviet-era S-300 air defense missiles as improvised ballistic ground-attack munitions carries significant accuracy limitations but has been used by Russia against civilian and infrastructure targets throughout the war, particularly after depletion of precision-guided ground-attack missiles. The dam strike risked further flooding along the Vovcha River and potential damage to agricultural land. The incident followed Russia's unprecedented May 24 Oreshnik IRBM strike on Bila Tserkva and represented a pattern of targeting Ukrainian water and energy infrastructure.

media.caption: Russia strikes Donetsk dam with S-300 missile, flooding villages along Vovcha River — May 25, 2026

title: Ukraine Strikes Vtorovo Oil Pumping Station in Vladimir Oblast — Supplies Moscow Airports
detail: On the night of May 23–24, 2026, Ukraine's SBU Special Group Alpha drone operators struck the Vtorovo oil pumping and dispatching station in Vladimir Oblast, approximately 650 km from the Ukrainian border, northeast of Moscow. The station, operated by JSC Transneft Verkhnyaya Volga (Russia's state oil pipeline monopoly), pumps diesel directly into the Moscow Ring Oil Product Pipeline and supplies fuel to Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo, and Vnukovo airports — the three major airports serving the Russian capital. A large fire covering approximately 800 square meters erupted at the facility, with heavy smoke visible by 7 a.m. on May 24. No casualties were reported. The facility had been struck previously in September 2025. Ukraine framed the attack as part of its 'long-range sanctions' campaign aimed at degrading Russia's domestic fuel supply chains and economic war capacity. The strike came on the same night as Russia's massive 600-drone/90-missile assault on Kyiv that used an Oreshnik IRBM — demonstrating simultaneous offensive and defensive asymmetric operations.

title: Russian Cumulative Losses Reach ~1,356,940 Personnel — 173 Combat Engagements on Day 1,551
detail: As of May 25, 2026 — Day 1,551 of Russia's full-scale invasion — Ukraine's General Staff reported total Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022 reached approximately 1,356,940 personnel, with approximately 1,020 losses recorded in the May 25 reporting period. Equipment losses on May 25 included 1,924 UAVs and 47 artillery systems. Ukrainian forces recorded 173 combat engagements along the front line on May 25, with the heaviest fighting in the Pokrovsk sector (32 Russian assaults) and the Huliaipole axis. Russian forces advanced in the Kostyantynivka-Druzhkivka area; Ukrainian forces advanced in the Hulyaipole direction. The frontline data comes against the backdrop of ISW noting that Russian forces suffered a net loss of 69 square miles of Ukrainian territory in April–May 2026 — the first net Russian territorial loss since August 2024. April 2026 saw 35,203 Russian losses — the sixth consecutive month losses exceeded recruitment capacity, with Russia continuing to compensate through forced mobilization and financial incentives.
